route: Non-lucrative residence visa (residencia no lucrativa). Consulate rule (Sao Paulo, point 7): "Seguro público o privado de enfermedad concertado con una Entidad aseguradora autorizada para operar en España ... debe de ser un seguro médico sin carencias, ni copago y sin límite de cobertura." London: "Public or private health insurance taken out by an insurance company authorised to operate in Spain." No-copayment/no-waiting-period wording is therefore consulate-specific but is the common standard.
policy: Sanitas Residents Visado, 2 insured, both age 45-49, rest of Spain, April 2026 tariff for new policies. Sold as a visa-grade policy: no waiting periods, no co-payments, repatriation (Sanitas visa page). Full-cover private health insurance valid in Spain. After the visa the couple can instead join the public system via the Convenio Especial after one year of registered residence: EUR 60 per person per month (under 65), so EUR 120 for two, no co-payments or waiting periods, but outpatient medicines are paid 100% by the patient.
working: 118.74 EUR per insured per month x 2 = 237.48. Plus Consorcio de Compensación de Seguros surcharge 0.15% (0.36) = 237.84 EUR a month. Convenio Especial route after year one: 60 x 2 = 120 EUR a month.

eu_citizen_difference: An EU citizen who is not working also needs private cover or an S1 to register as a resident, and joins the Convenio Especial on the same terms. After five years of legal residence EU citizens and their non-EU family acquire permanent residence and free access to the public system without the agreement (Sanidad page). A UK S1 holder is accepted by the London consulate in place of insurance (an S1 is for pensioners, so not this couple).

spot_check: No second insurer tariff retrieved. Sanitas own visa page says its International Residents product starts 'desde 95,15 EUR/mes' (per person, age not stated), consistent in order of magnitude with 118.74 at age 45-49. The Sanitas Mas Salud 'Sin copago' product in Madrid, age 45-49, 2-3 insureds, costs 124.02 per person but carries waiting periods, so it would not meet the visa rule. Comparison sites (flagged, not used) give 65 to 150 EUR per person at age 45.
uncertainty: Single insurer. I assumed the '2 asegurados' cell is a per-person premium; if it is the premium for the pair, the figure would be about 119 EUR, half. Consulate wording varies, and some consulates also ask for repatriation, which the Visado product includes. New-business premium for year one; renewals rise with age band (50-54 band: 127.38 x 2 for Visado 2 insured, Resto) and with claims-inflation. Some insurers may sell cheaper visa-grade products (an Adeslas or Asisa tariff was not retrieved), so the true cheapest could be 10 to 30% lower.
